title: Extraction and Sequencing of High Molecular Weight Genomic DNA from Auxenochlorella protothecoides
author: Dimitrios J. Camacho
materials: Do not inhale phenol and/or chloroform. Perform all work with phenol and chloroform in a fume hood (parts of steps 10–16). Tubes containing phenol and/or chloroform should only be opened in the fume hood. Decant the solution to a 15 mL phase-lock gel tube (QIAGEN MaXtract). Use a serological pipette to carefully pierce through the top layer of TRIS and draw up the phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol from the bottom the layer. Add 2 mL of room temperature phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) . Mix by gentle inversion (~40 turns per minute) for 5 min.
Bring all SRE kit solutions to room temperature. Set the centrifuge to 29 °C .

Thaw or chill all reagents on wet ice: Nuclease free water DNA NEBNext FFPE DNA Repair Buffer v2 NEBNext FFPE DNA Repair Mix Ultra II End-prep Enzyme Mix Freshly prepared 80% ethanol Thaw an aliquot of AMPure XP Beads at room temperature. Flick all tubes to mix. Do not vortex tubes.
Thaw the following reagents at room temperature: Sequencing Buffer (SB) Library Beads (LIB) Flow Cell Tether (FCT) Flow Cell Flush (FCF) Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) Vortex and spin down all tubes.
Pause the sequencing run on the MinKNOW software.

Open the MinKNOW software on your computer. The software will fail to launch if the computer is not connected to the internet. Telemetry data is shared with ONT and offline MinKNOW operation should be requested from ONT in advance. MinKNOW Home Screen. Click on "Start" icon to the left and click on "Start sequencing" highlighted in green.

steps.title: Grow algae to mid‑log
steps.instruction: Cultivate Auxenochlorella protothecoides in liquid medium until the culture reaches mid‑log phase (≈1 × 10⁷ cells · mL⁻¹). Determine the required volume to harvest >1 × 10⁸ cells.

steps.title: Add proteinase K and RNase A
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL proteinase K (20 mg · mL⁻¹) and 25 µL DNase‑free RNase A (20 mg · mL⁻¹) to the cell suspension, mix by gentle inversion, and incubate at 65 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Freeze‑grind cells with liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Using a spoil board, place a ceramic mortar and pestle on the bench, fill with liquid nitrogen, and chill by repeating addition of LN₂ until boiling ceases (3–5 ×). Add the cell suspension dropwise (using a P1000 with a wide‑orifice tip) into the LN₂; each drop freezes instantly. Lightly tap the mortar to prevent fragments from flying out, re‑apply LN₂ as needed, then grind slowly in a circular motion until the material resembles green matcha powder.

steps.title: Collect frozen powder
steps.instruction: Scrape the resulting powder into a 50 mL Falcon tube with a plastic spatula.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 µL nuclease‑free water by gentle pipette mixing (wide‑orifice or cut tip).

steps.title: Centrifuge culture
steps.instruction: Transfer up to 45 mL liquid culture to a 50 mL Diamond Max centrifuge tube, place in a fixed‑angle JA‑14.50 rotor (Beckman Coulter Avanti JXN‑26), and centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 2 min at room temperature. Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Quantify and normalize DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a broad‑range dsDNA Qubit. Dilute/adjust the sample to ≈150 ng · µL⁻¹ in a final volume of 60 µL using nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Magnetic bead cleanup – bind DNA
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic rack for 5 min (or until the supernatant is clear). Transfer the clear supernatant containing DNA to a new 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tube.

steps.title: Equilibrate beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend the magnetic beads in 60 µL nuclease‑free water and incubate at room temperature for at least 30 min.

steps.title: Ethanol wash #1
steps.instruction: Remove the tube from the magnetic rack, pulse‑centrifuge the pellet, pipette off residual ethanol, and dry the pellet for 30 s–1 min (≤5 µL ethanol may remain).

steps.title: Add 70 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL 70 % ethanol to the tube (still on the magnetic rack), wait 1 min, then remove the supernatant.

steps.title: Second magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the tube on the magnetic rack for 5 min, wait until the supernatant is clear, and discard it.

steps.title: Add AMPure XP beads
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (100 µL) of AMPure XP beads (pre‑equilibrated to room temperature and vortexed 10 s), mix gently by hand for 5 min.

steps.title: Combine bead‑DNA suspensions
steps.instruction: Gently pipette the contents of three tubes into the fourth tube (the one containing the majority of DNA precipitate) to combine all material.

steps.title: Overnight pellet resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the combined pellet overnight in 25 µL ultrapure water.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash after decanting
steps.instruction: After decanting most supernatant following the second wash, pulse‑centrifuge, then dry the pellet in a laminar‑flow hood for ~5 min.

steps.title: 70 % ethanol wash (high‑speed)
steps.instruction: Discard supernatant, add 1 mL freshly prepared 70 % ethanol, invert gently, centrifuge at 20 000 × g for 1 min (same centrifuge and rotor as step 7), discard supernatant and repeat once.

steps.title: High‑speed spin of DNA mixture
steps.instruction: Decant the mixture (including any precipitates) into four 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tubes and centrifuge at 20 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C using the FA‑45‑24‑11 2 mL fixed‑angle rotor (Eppendorf 5424R).

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with ethanol
steps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous phase to a new 15 mL Falcon tube, add 2 × volume (4 mL) ice‑cold 100 % ethanol, invert 10 times, and incubate on ice for 1 h.

steps.title: Chloroform:isoamyl wash #1
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1), mix gently by inversion for 5 min, then centrifuge at 1 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Centrifugation repeat
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube again at 1 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Phenol:chloroform:isoamyl wash
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL room‑temperature phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1), mix by gentle inversion (~40 turns · min⁻¹) for 5 min.

steps.title: Proteinase K / RNase A treatment
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL proteinase K and 25 µL RNase A to the aqueous phase in a new MaXtract phase‑lock tube, mix gently by inversion, and incubate at 37 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: Phase‑lock centrifugation
steps.instruction: Ensure MaXtract High‑Density tubes are prepared, centrifuge at 1 500 × g for 5 min at room temperature (Eppendorf 5810 R, rotor A‑4‑81). If phases are not clearly separated, centrifuge an additional 2 min. Set the centrifuge to 4 °C, then decant the top aqueous layer to a new 15 mL phase‑lock gel tube. Set the gel tubes aside in phenol/chloroform waste.

steps.title: Incubate at 50 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the aqueous phase tube at 50 °C for 1 h in a water bath or heating block.

steps.title: Add SRE buffer
steps.instruction: Add 60 µL SRE buffer to the sample and invert several times to mix.

steps.title: Final DNA quality control
steps.instruction: Measure A260/A230 and A260/A280 ratios with a Nanodrop, determine concentration with Qubit, and assess fragment size distribution by gel electrophoresis or femto‑pulse capillary electrophoresis. Expected yield ≈6 µg (60 %–85 % of starting DNA).

steps.title: Add Buffer LTE
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL Buffer LTE, incubate at room temperature for 20 min, and flick the tube to fully resuspend the pellet. Optional: store DNA at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Using a P200 pipette, carefully remove the supernatant (up to 10 µL liquid may remain; the pellet may be invisible).

steps.title: High‑speed spin of ligation mix
steps.instruction: Load the tube into a centrifuge with the hinge facing outward and spin at 10 000 × g for 30 min at 29 °C.

steps.title: Prepare ligation reagents on ice
steps.instruction: Spin down Ligation Adapter (LA) and Salt‑T4 DNA Ligase, place on wet ice. Thaw Ligation Buffer, Elution Buffer, and Long Fragment Buffer at room temperature, vortex the latter two, and keep all reagents on wet ice.

steps.title: Assemble sequencing mix
steps.instruction: In a new 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tube, add 37.5 µL Sequencing Buffer, resuspend Library Beads, add 25.5 µL Library Beads to the buffer, then add 12 µL DNA (from step 22).

steps.title: Magnetic clean‑up of sequencing mix
steps.instruction: Spin the tube briefly, place on a magnetic rack until the supernatant is clear, keep on the magnet, and carefully pipette off the supernatant.

steps.title: Gentle inversion mixing
steps.instruction: Mix the sample by gentle inversion for 5 min (~40 turns · min⁻¹).

steps.title: Add AMPure beads to end‑prep
steps.instruction: Vortex AMPure XP beads to resuspend, add 60 µL beads to the end‑prep reaction, and mix by flicking.

steps.title: Transfer end‑prep reaction
steps.instruction: Move the end‑prep reaction to a clean 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tube.

steps.title: Thermal cycling of end‑prep
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction in a thermal cycler at 20 °C for 5 min then 65 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: DNA repair and end‑prep mix
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 µg DNA to a 0.2 mL PCR tube, bring volume to 47 µL with chilled nuclease‑free water, then add sequentially: 7 µL NEBNext FFPE DNA Repair Buffer v2, 2 µL NEBNext FFPE DNA Repair Mix, 3 µL Ultra II End‑prep Enzyme Mix. After each addition, flick gently and give a quick spin.

steps.title: Ethanol wash of beads
steps.instruction: Slowly add 200 µL freshly prepared 80 % ethanol to the bead pellet without disturbing it.

steps.title: Second magnetic ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant, spin briefly, place tube back on the magnetic rack, remove residual ethanol (do not let the pellet dry >1 min; one wash is sufficient).

steps.title: Elution with nuclease‑free water
steps.instruction: Remove the tube from the magnetic rack, add 61 µL room‑temperature nuclease‑free water, and incubate at 37 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Final magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the tube back on the magnetic rack, wait until beads form a compact pellet and the supernatant is clear.

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: Transfer the clear supernatant to a clean 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tube.

steps.title: Quantify post‑repair DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a Qubit fluorometer; expect ~50 % recovery of the concentration measured in step 22.

steps.title: Optional storage of DNA
steps.instruction: Proceed immediately to the next step or store the DNA at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Final library QC
steps.instruction: Quantify DNA again with Qubit and assess fragment size distribution by gel electrophoresis or femto‑pulse capillary electrophoresis.

steps.title: Magnetic clean‑up before elution
steps.instruction: Place the tube on the magnetic rack until the supernatant is colorless, then transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tube.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Remove the tube from the magnetic rack, add 15 µL Elution Buffer, and incubate at 37 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Long fragment buffer wash
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL Long Fragment Buffer, flick to mix, spin, place on magnetic rack, wait for clear supernatant, remove supernatant, use a P20 to remove residual ethanol, and dry the pellet for <30 s (≤5 µL ethanol may remain). Do not over‑dry.

steps.title: Final magnetic bead removal
steps.instruction: Spin down the sample, place on the magnetic rack, wait until the solution is clear, and pipette off the supernatant.

steps.title: Add AMPure beads for final cleanup
steps.instruction: Add 40 µL resuspended AMPure XP beads to the reaction, mix by gentle inversion for 5 min at room temperature (≈40 inversions · min⁻¹).

steps.title: Ligation adapter addition
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL Ligation Adapter to the 60 µL DNA eluate (from step 48), flick to mix, then add 25 µL Ligation Buffer and flick, followed by 10 µL Salt‑T4 DNA Ligase and flick. Incubate at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Prime flow cell – open port
steps.instruction: Open the flow‑cell priming port by sliding the cover clockwise.

steps.title: Connect sequencing device
steps.instruction: Connect the Mk1B sequencing device to a computer (device powers on when connected). Open the Mk1B lid, slide the MinION flow cell under the clip, ensuring the two guide pins engage the pins on the device, and press lightly to secure thermal and electrical contact.

steps.title: Prepare flow‑cell flush solution
steps.instruction: In a new 1.5 mL nuclease‑free tube, add 1170 µL Flow Cell Flush, 5 µL Bovine Serum Albumin, and 30 µL Flow Cell Tether Mix; mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Check for air bubbles in priming port
steps.instruction: Inspect the priming port for air bubbles. If present, set a P1000 to 200 µL, attach a clean tip, insert into the port, and turn the dial to 220–230 µL to draw up 20–30 µL, removing the bubble. Do not draw more than 30 µL.

steps.title: Load priming solution
steps.instruction: Load 800 µL of the priming solution (from step 61) into the priming port, avoiding air bubbles by keeping a small volume in the tip and not depressing past the second stop. Wait 5 min.

steps.title: Dilute library to 300 ng
steps.instruction: Dilute the library to 300 ng in 12 µL (25 ng · µL⁻¹) using Elution Buffer.

steps.title: Load library onto SpotON port
steps.instruction: Mix the diluted library gently by pipetting up and down, then slowly add 75 µL dropwise to the SpotON sample port, allowing each drop to flow before adding the next.

steps.title: Prime SpotON port with wash mix
steps.instruction: Lift the SpotON sample port cover, load 200 µL of the priming mix into the flow‑cell priming port (not the SpotON port), replace the SpotON cover, close the priming port, and place the light shield above the sensor array. Close the MinION lid.

steps.title: Prepare wash reagents
steps.instruction: Place a tube of Wash Mix on ice (do not vortex). Thaw a tube of Wash Diluent at room temperature, vortex to mix, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prime flow cell again (second priming)
steps.instruction: Open the Mk1B lid, slide open the priming port cover clockwise, verify no air bubbles (step 64), then proceed with the priming steps (steps 63–66) to prime the flow cell. During the 5 min incubation, warm the recovered DNA library to room temperature.

steps.title: Load recovered library after priming
steps.instruction: After priming, open the SpotON sample port and add ~150 µL of the recovered room‑temperature DNA library dropwise.

steps.title: Start sequencing run
steps.instruction: Close the SpotON sample port and the MinION lid, then start the sequencing run in the MinKNOW software.

steps.title: Wash flow cell (optional reuse)
steps.instruction: Add ~400 µL of Flow Cell Wash Mix (from step 81) into the priming port (do not add all at once; leave some liquid in the tip to avoid bubbles). Follow steps 63–66 again to prime the flow cell, warming the recovered library during the 5 min incubation.

steps.title: Final flow‑cell closure
steps.instruction: Close both the priming port cover and the SpotON sample port cover to ensure no air enters the sensor array.
